readback_body:
## Requirements: Conversation-inspired, Session-first Web Sidebar redesign

### Context and decision
Current `WebLayout → Sidebar → SidebarAgents + SessionListHeader + SessionList + SidebarFooter` leads with infrastructure and consumes the prime navigation area with non-actionable Agent rows. The resulting information hierarchy feels like an administration dashboard rather than a return-to-work navigator. The user requested a redesign referencing Claude and ChatGPT sidebars.

This is a **new navigation and presentation decision**, not a recurrence of the old #1195 width bug or #1196 one-button-rail bug. It intentionally **supersedes the older #748/#1196 expanded/sidebar anatomy** while retaining their proven shell-state/geometry/Terminal-continuity boundaries. Current `main` is a baseline, not the candidate UI.

References:
- `VISION.md`, `PRINCIPLE.md`, `PRODUCT.md`; `docs/design/{information-architecture,composition,interaction/web}.md` and `docs/design/design-system/patterns/session-list.md`.
- `web/src/app/experiences/web/WebLayout.tsx`, `web/src/app/Sidebar.tsx`, `web/src/app/patterns/{SidebarAgents,SidebarRail,SessionListHeader}.tsx`, `web/src/app/SessionDrawer.tsx`.
- Claude/ChatGPT as **interaction precedents** (fast new-work/search, quiet typography, recent work and secondary settings), not as a domain model, product branding or permission to introduce permanent feature catalogs.

### Target IA and visual composition
Desktop, expanded (candidate):
```text
┌────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┐
│ [Sidebar toggle] [ + New ] │                                │
│ [ Search sessions...     ] │                                │
│                            │                                │
│ Sessions                   │   Current Session work surface │
│ Today                      │   Terminal / Workspace         │
│   ● Fix terminal reconnect │                                │
│     Claude Code · devbox   │                                │
│   ● Improve Files          │                                │
│     shell · macbook        │                                │
│ Earlier                    │                                │
│     Production shell       │                                │
│                            │                                │
│ [Agents / locations]       │                                │
│ [Server connectivity]      │                                │
└────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘
```
- **Session is first**: Sessions are a flat list, optionally separated by recency (Today / Earlier), never parented under Agent. A conversation-like row is a visual/reference pattern, **not** a chat-message object or AI-specific Session schema.
- **Top**: one stable toggle, one explicit New Session action, quick search. Keep the search scope Sessions; preserve existing filter/sort semantics through secondary disclosure where useful, rather than permanently exposing a filter toolbar.
- **Rows / unified action entry**: one-line display title (metadata alias if set), restrained workload/location metadata and locally meaningful reachability. On **wide and narrow Web**, one row-anchored `···` dropdown contains `Session details`, `Edit details`, `Attach settings`, `Kill session`; no desktop inline gear/trash actions. Wide Web reveals the trigger on hover/focus/selection; narrow Web retains a 44px touch target. The menu overlays the list; it never replaces the list or silently selects a Session. Existing SessionDetails/SessionMetadataSection own read/edit metadata (Title / Description / Tags), AttachDialog owns configure, KillConfirmDialog owns typed exact **tmux Session name** confirmation. Edit changes the display alias, never tmux identity or session_id. Offline metadata editing is unavailable; read-only details remain accessible. Kill is visually separated as destructive. No extra per-Agent decoration, giant badges or stacked cards.
- **Secondary infrastructure**: do not lead with a static Agent roster. Provide a compact discoverable Agents/locations entry in the lower region that can reveal detail on demand; keep Server connection status separate from Agent, Session lifecycle and attachment state. Not all Agents being online must not make the global Server indicator red.
- **Collapse**: explore the Claude/ChatGPT fully-tucked-away pattern: wide Web sidebar returns **all** its reserved width to current work, with a visible minimal top-edge reopening control in the work shell. Do not keep redundant clickable rail icons or a 52px navigation bar by default; no new permanent work-surface header. Collapse state remains `WebLayout`-owned, selection/search/scroll stay intact and attached Terminal is not remounted.
- **Narrow Web**: existing overlay `SessionDrawer` with a clear close path, no desktop rail. **App**: its separate `Sessions ← Terminal → Workspace` spatial model survives; this is not an instruction to import desktop sidebar into App.
- No universal Projects/Workspace hierarchy before the logical Workspace identity is actually available. If added later, it must have explicit semantic identity and must not make selecting a Session require navigating a project folder.
- Do not add Nession wordmark/top branding band as an incidental ChatGPT copy. A new permanent header requires a separate justified product decision.

### Session action UX: approved candidate revision (all Web viewports)

The new design changes the **entry point**, not the underlying Session API. Current main `SessionItem.tsx` uses wide-Web inline Settings/Kill icons and a two-item narrow `DropdownMenu`. Per this review, the candidate consistently uses one **`···` dropdown** on wide and narrow Web. It contains four entries: **Session details**, **Edit details**, **Attach settings**, and **Kill session** (separator before Kill).

- **Read/edit details** expose existing `SessionDetails` / `SessionMetadataSection` capabilities from #2789. Title (display alias), description and tags belong to Session metadata; re-use the existing Agent-owned persistence, validation, cache and revision semantics. Do not rename tmux or introduce new backend methods.
- **Attach settings** reuses `AttachDialog` with configure intent.
- **Kill** reuses `KillConfirmDialog` and requires typing the immutable tmux Session name, not an optional display alias.
- The dropdown is a floating anchored **menu**, not a full-sidebar replacement or an action in itself. Click-outside, list scroll and Escape dismiss it; keyboard/focus follow Nession's menu primitive. Offline Agent prevents metadata save but not viewing details.
- The prototype uses local overlays for review; production must connect the existing editors/dialog owners rather than copy fixture code.

### High-fidelity UI design specification

Required design handoff for this UI-facing Requirement is **IA / interactions + exact visual metrics + browser-rendered fidelity**, not just a clickable HTML navigation flow.

**Presentation requirement:** Visual UI specifications must be **visible and inspectable within the interactive prototype's review page**, not only linked to a Markdown file. The [in-page UI spec inspector](https://bestnathan.github.io/nession/prototypes/sidebar-session-first-2851/index.html#ui-spec) contains a live Sidebar/work width ruler, component picker/direct preview selection, computed geometry/type metrics, token references, and color/type samples. Review-only annotation must stay outside the measured product viewport. The Markdown specification is supporting source and rationale, not the sole UI design artifact.

The source-of-truth is the project's generated Design Token API and actual Product Pattern contracts. The candidate [UI-SPEC.md](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/c023c84dc7087dcd2b23577d0d5e4c21e0f16c21/sidebar-session-first-2851/UI-SPEC.md) pins the main baseline at `0f3b2a012a9203a68ca5f38d56dd1393f6cf74b0`, documenting Token → computed value → candidate rule → state/viewport verification.

Key existing Web metrics: sidebar `--nession-shell-sidebar-width = 246px`; shell icon control `--nession-shell-icon-button-size = 36px`; Session primary font **14px / 550**, metadata **11.5px / 475**; Session row padding **7px vertical and 8px horizontal** (no hardcoded total row height); row radius **7px**; server status mark **5px**; control radius **10px**; shell motion **180ms** with canonical easing. Colors, focus rings and typography roles use Nession generated semantic tokens, not a second palette.

**Explicit novel candidate values:** top-actions group minimum **52px** is derived from existing 36px control + 8px top/bottom and must not be mistaken for a global Nession header-band token. Wide-Web collapsed geometry **0px** intentionally changes the old 50px rail contract. Narrow Web uses the shipped `SessionDrawer` width `min(20rem,90vw)` and remains separate from App's 44px minimum tap-target model.

**Verification:** Canonical Web **1280×800 and 1440×900** plus optional 1180/1024 probes; narrow-Web 390×844 and 375×812. Chromium/Playwright must measure bounding boxes, computed typography/line-height, spacing, radii, colors and focus state; check selected/hover/empty/offline/error states, collapse work-width reclamation, keyboard and scroll ownership. Compare unchanged controls with actual product fixtures. The prototype's Terminal is a text approximation, **not** pixel-matched xterm. A 1:1 CSS-pixel viewport is not visual parity evidence.

### Component ownership and implementation guardrails
- `WebLayout` owns column geometry/collapse; `Sidebar` owns presentation/composition; `SessionList/SessionItem` own Session identity/selection semantics; contextual Agent detail remains a separate product capability.
- Reuse design tokens, Nession shell patterns and shadcn primitives; do not copy vendor DOM or assets.
- **Menu integration:** extend existing `SessionItem` and its anchored `DropdownMenu` for wide/narrow Web, reuse `SessionDetails` / `SessionMetadataSection` for work metadata, and `ShellDialogs` for configure/kill. Menu items are adapters to current capabilities, not a new Session API.
- Migrate design contracts/golden screenshots and relevant `docs/design/` owner in the same **production** change; do not edit production owners in the prototype-only branch.
- Preserve active Session attachment, xterm content and viewport geometry after expand/collapse. Preserve disconnected Session rows and draft search/filter state after collapse/reopen.
- Responsive behavior must be driven by **actual product container width**, not review-page browser width.

### Prototype
- **Decision:** Required (new navigation information hierarchy + Web collapsed/narrow tradeoff).
- **Question:** Is a conversations-inspired Session list easier to scan while keeping infrastructure discoverable but quiet? Is full tuck-away preferable to the historical static rail?
- **Scenario:** Open work → switch/search Sessions → use row `···` menu → inspect details → edit display metadata → configure attach settings → exercise typed-name Kill confirmation → collapse/reopen → narrow Web drawer → repeat menu; inspect offline Agent and empty states.
- **Status:** Unified anchored `···` Session action dropdown now represented on desktop and narrow Web in prototype, with local view/edit metadata, configure and typed-name Kill flows plus in-page high-fidelity inspector. Source committed to shared `prototype` branch. Pages deployment and Chromium browser validation remain unverified.
- **Interactive prototype (preview candidate, NOT YET VERIFIED LIVE):** https://bestnathan.github.io/nession/prototypes/sidebar-session-first-2851/index.html
- **Embedded visual UI Spec (same HTML page):** https://bestnathan.github.io/nession/prototypes/sidebar-session-first-2851/index.html#ui-spec — choose an element or enable preview inspection; live DOM geometry, Token references, color/type samples and layout ruler are visible in the prototype review UI. **Pages deployment remains unverified.**
- **Immutable source pin:** https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/c023c84dc7087dcd2b23577d0d5e4c21e0f16c21/sidebar-session-first-2851/index.html
- **High-fidelity UI specification:** https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/c023c84dc7087dcd2b23577d0d5e4c21e0f16c21/sidebar-session-first-2851/UI-SPEC.md
- **Scenario/fidelity and test plan:** https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/c023c84dc7087dcd2b23577d0d5e4c21e0f16c21/sidebar-session-first-2851/README.md
- **Published branch revision:** `c023c84dc7087dcd2b23577d0d5e4c21e0f16c21` (only source confirmed; match against Pages manifest SHA before claiming public update).
- **Fidelity:** 1280/1440 canonical Web, 1180/1024 exploratory Web, and 390/375 narrow-Web CSS-pixel selectors, simulated Session/Agent data, token-aligned Sidebar styling and a basic Terminal/Workspace approximation only; no real WebSocket, Agent, tmux, terminal attach, backend creation, browser-tested fidelity or production Acceptance.

### Success Criteria
- [ ] SC-01 Wide Web sidebar begins with Session navigation, search and explicit New Session, without Agent roster or capability directory permanently occupying the top of the list; flat Session identity is legible and current Session selected.
- [ ] SC-02 Search, select, empty/error states and the **same row `···` dropdown on wide and narrow Web** are keyboard-/pointer-operable. The anchored menu exposes all four actions (`Session details`, `Edit details`, `Attach settings`, `Kill session`), retains the Session list and selected work, and dismisses by Escape/outside click/list scroll. View details reads the target Session without selecting it; edit title/description/tags reuses the current metadata owner and never renames tmux. Configure uses existing attach settings; Kill requires typed immutable tmux Session name. Offline Sessions remain discoverable, editing unavailability is explicit and no Conversation semantics are invented.
- [ ] SC-03 Expand/collapse really changes the reserved navigation column width, keeps an operable reopen affordance, preserves selected Session and existing Terminal mount, and does not introduce extra permanent chrome.
- [ ] SC-04 Narrow Web uses an overlay drawer with close/selection behavior and no rail; App spatial Sessions layer remains independent of Web collapse.
- [ ] SC-05 Server status is not aggregated from Agent online/session lifecycle/attachment states; Agent context is explicitly reachable without forming a required Session hierarchy.

- [ ] SC-06 At canonical Web viewports, the implemented Sidebar renders Nession's approved metrics (246px expanded column, 36px icon controls, 14px Session title, 11.5px metadata, 7px row radius and 5px status mark), and an executed Chromium Case checks computed geometry, representative interactive states and accessibility against the pinned UI Spec.

### SC → scenario and evidence plan
- SC-01..SC-06: **SCN-02 Web/App interaction and visual**. Approved Chromium + Playwright browser Cases on deterministic product fixture, desktop width and representative narrow Web/App viewport, keyboard/pointer/emulated touch, DOM roles/accessibility, computed geometry and screenshots. The source-aligned Cases execute at the exact staging merge SHA, where the trusted `Acceptance / Cases` lane can authenticate and project their records; pre-merge Case Smoke remains a smoke check, not Acceptance evidence. Existing `e2e/tests/browser/ui-contract-web.spec.ts` / `fixture-visual.spec.ts` and `fixture-visual-app.spec.ts` are regression references, not automatic evidence; the Cases carry targeted assertions. No additional staging integration beyond the Case lane and no Full E2E are required for this scoped shell redesign.

## Product alignment
- [x] Work-first: Session navigation remains the primary return-to-work entry.
- [x] Progressive disclosure: infrastructure and capability catalogs are secondary/on demand.
- [x] Desktop collapse cedes geometry to the work surface.
- [x] Web vs App independent interactions.
